summary: The most addictive Klondike Solitaire game in the world!
description:
Experience classic fun and the thrill of victory all in one place! Discover the most beloved solitaire card game now
With simple rules and intuitive gameplay, anyone can easily enjoy it, regardless of age
Bring new life to the game with customizable solitaire features
Once you play, you'll clearly feel the difference
Play anytime, anywhere to train your brain and relieve stress effortlessly

[How to Play]
- Klondike Solitaire is a card/board game similar to Cube, Freecell, Spider, Tri Peaks, Pyramid, Golf, and Mahjong.
- The game is played using a standard deck of 52 cards, excluding jokers.
- Cards must be stacked in the foundation piles in order from Ace (A) to King (K) by suit.
- There are a total of 4 foundation piles, and each pile must only contain cards of the same suit.
- Cards in the tableau must be stacked in descending order (King to Ace) alternating colors (red and black).
- Only a King (K) card can be placed in an empty column.
- The top card or a stack of cards from one column can be moved to another.
- Cards moved to another column must follow the alternating color rule and be in descending order from King to Ace.
- You win the game by moving all the cards to the foundation piles.

[Features]
- Offline play
- Various modes including Daily Challenges and Events
- Option to select one-card deal or three-card deal
- Unlimited free undo
- Unlimited free hints
- Detailed play statistics
- Supports both standard scoring and Vegas scoring
- Left-hand mode support
- Freedom to customize card fronts and backs as you like
- Supports various themed backgrounds
- Free play without heart or move limitations
- Tablet device support

[Play Tips]
- Prioritize moving cards to the foundation pile.
- Once all hidden cards are revealed, winning becomes easier.
- Focus on clearing columns with the most hidden cards first.
- Don’t always organize open cards into one column. Sometimes leaving them across multiple columns makes it easier to win.
